SECTION III
PROJECT IMPACTS AND MITIGATION MEASURES
A. LAND USE AND ZONING
Implementation of the three-year Community Development Block Grant Program will have no substantial or long lasting effects on land use in San Jose. The main thrust of the CDBG program is the revitalization of older, existing residential neighborhoods. Rehabilitation will involve: 1. Interim assistance to alleviate harmful conditions in which immediate public action is needed; and 2. Financing rehabilitation of privately owned properties. It will alter the quality and present character of the designated neighborhoods without changing the existing land use. Such comprehensive rehabilitation effort as are proposed will serve to prevent the decline of older neighborhoods, with a high percentage of substandard units, from experiencing the blight which eventaully destroys a residential area. The central core area of cities often experiences the decline of single-family neighborhoods and their gradually and irreversible evolution into mixed and incompatible uses. Associated with such decline is the need for more housing elsewhere in the city. The CDBG program will continue its current efforts at neighborhood preservation. This will have a positive impact in two ways: Existing residential area will not change their land use character; and new residential development elsewhere in the city will not be required to offset the loss of an older neighborhood.
Only one CDBG project will have a direct land use impact: the construction of the Alma Neighborhood Center will alter the existing land use to the degree that vacant land will support a new building. The impact is negligible.
The CDBG program plans the use of loans and grants for all the target neighborhoods except Alma and Alviso. These loans and grants will enable individual property owners to make improvements to their dwelling units which will correct substandard construction or fixtures, make the dwelling meet applicable housing codes, and generally increase the livability and longevity of the house. Beyond the specific neighborhoods identified, the CDBG program provides funds for home improvements in the Central and the Alum Rock Planning Areas in general.
Additional CDBG programs aim at improving the public facility infrastructure of all seven target CNRA's. These improvements will include street reconstruction

The San Jose Housing Code (Ordinance No. 18530) provides minimum requirements for the protection of life, limb, health, property, safety, and welfare of the general public and the owners and occupants of existing residential buildings. It is distinct from the Building Code which governs the construction of new dwelling units.
